title: 华尔街开始FOMO了！加密下一轮造富，散户还有先手？｜Jordi Vissel

keyPoints.text: Bitcoin demonstrated resilience by not falling despite multiple negative headwinds such as rate hikes, cold wallet issues, and the failure of regulatory clarity legislation, subsequently surging upon slight positive news.
Crypto infrastructure such as Bitcoin and Ethereum is at an inflection point analogous to the launch of the iPhone, where AI digital agents represent the catalyst to utilize the existing rails.

Technological divergence causes digital and AI-driven businesses to expand while traditional businesses lag under high interest rates and financing costs, leading Wall Street funds to seek crypto and digital opportunities.
Digital economy tech leaders persistently outperform traditional sectors, which face headwinds from interest rates, financing costs, and compressed demand.
The 2021-2022 crypto boom built out foundational Layer 1 and Layer 2 infrastructure analogous to the dot-com bubble, which AI agents and novel applications are now positioned to utilize.
Retail investors have a strategic advantage in researching emerging tokens before 2027, when institutional coverage is expected to expand aggressively beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Wall Street fund managers overseeing tens to hundreds of billions in assets are experiencing FOMO and actively inquiring about getting into crypto and tokenization of assets, while retail investors had already turned aggressively bullish earlier.
Bitcoin surged from approximately 58,000–64,000 to around 84,000 (roughly a 40% gain) following earlier commentary on Joe Dispenza.

Wall Street is experiencing FOMO around crypto and asset tokenization after missing out on previous semiconductor moves like Micron, potentially escalating institutional allocations from exploratory 1% allocations to $10 billion to $20 billion or more.
AI agents requiring transaction privacy may drive adoption of privacy coins such as Zcash (ZEC), potentially driving multi-fold price increases.

mainTopics: Bitcoin Price Movements and Market Resilience
AI Agents and Blockchain Infrastructure Utilization
sentences: The speaker notes that Bitcoin traded around 58,000 to 64,000 before surging to around 84,000, which is mentioned as approximately a 40 percent gain.

The commentary highlights that Bitcoin exhibited resilience by not falling on negative news such as rate hikes, cold wallet issues, and the failure of regulatory clarity legislation, subsequently reaching 84,500.
The source notes that after Trump remarked on supporting crypto at a press conference, Bitcoin advanced from 64,000 to approximately 75,000.
The speaker references expectations that dot plot predictions indicated a potential 25 basis point interest rate hike.
The discussion draws an analogy between crypto infrastructure such as Bitcoin and Ethereum and the launch of the iPhone, asserting that AI digital agents serve as the catalyst to utilize these rails.

The 2021 to 2022 crypto cycle is compared to the dot-com bubble, leaving behind Layer 1, Layer 2, and decentralized exchange infrastructure like Hyperliquid that require applications to achieve sustained usage.
Technological divergence is cited as separating digital and AI-driven companies that expand continuously from traditional firms constrained by interest rates, financing costs, and demand.
The commentary mentions a scenario where AI agents requiring transaction confidentiality choose privacy coins such as Zcash (ZEC), resulting in price gains of more than tenfold.
The source reports that Wall Street managers overseeing 50 billion to 100 billion in assets are displaying FOMO regarding crypto and asset tokenization.

The video relates a proposal by host Pomp suggesting institutional allocations could shift from 1 percent testing allocations to 10 billion or 20 billion or more after having missed moves in Micron Technology.

Jody Visser expects that large-scale institutional research coverage of tokens beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum will not materialize until 2027, when projects such as ZEC, Solana, or Hyperliquid may be covered.

Borrowing Peter Lynch's framework, the speaker argues that retail investors maintain an informational advantage only before 2027 by researching specific tokens before large-scale institutional coverage and capital inflows occur.
